Input_Rate_Dist

Source: R/Input_Rate_Dist.R
Input_Rate_Dist.Rd

Calculate group-level category distributions (breakdowns) of a metric's numerator and/or denominator.

Usage

Input_Rate_Dist(
  dfSubjects,
  dfNumerator,
  dfDenominator,
  strGroupCol = "GroupID",
  strGroupLevel = NULL,
  strSubjectCol = "SubjectID",
  strNumeratorMethod = c("Count", "Sum"),
  strDenominatorMethod = c("Count", "Sum"),
  strNumeratorCol = NULL,
  strDenominatorCol = NULL,
  strNumeratorCatCols = NULL,
  strDenominatorCatCols = NULL,
  strCatDelim = NULL
)

Arguments

dfSubjects

data.frame with columns for SubjectID and any other relevant subject information

dfNumerator

data.frame with a column for SubjectID and strNumeratorCol if strNumeratorMethod is "Sum"

dfDenominator

data.frame with a column for SubjectID and strDenominatorCol if strDenominatorMethod is "Sum"

strGroupCol

character Column name in dfSubjects to use for grouping. Default: "GroupID"

strGroupLevel

character value for the group level. Default: NULL which is parsed to strGroupCol

strSubjectCol

character Column name in dfSubjects to use for subject ID. Default: "SubjectID"

strNumeratorMethod

character Method to calculate numerator. Default: "Count"

strDenominatorMethod

character Method to calculate denominator. Default: "Count"

strNumeratorCol

character Column name in dfNumerator to use for numerator calculation. Default: NULL

strDenominatorCol

character Column name in dfDenominator to use for denominator calculation. Default: NULL

strNumeratorCatCols

character Column name(s) in dfNumerator to break the numerator down by. Default: NULL (no numerator breakdowns).

strDenominatorCatCols

character Column name(s) in dfDenominator to break the denominator down by. Default: NULL (no denominator breakdowns).

strCatDelim

character Delimiter used to split multi-value category cells. Default: NULL (no splitting).

Value

data.frame with one row per group, source, variable and category, and the following specification:

Column NameDescriptionType
GroupIDThe group IDCharacter
GroupLevelThe group typeCharacter
Source"Numerator" or "Denominator"Character
VariableThe category column nameCharacter
CategoryThe category value; "Not recorded" when missing or blankCharacter
CountRecords (or summed values) in the categoryNumeric
ParticipantsDistinct subjects in the categoryInteger
TotalThe group's numerator or denominator from Input_Rate()Numeric
PercentCount / Total; NA when Total is 0Numeric

When no category columns are supplied, a zero-row data frame with these columns is returned.

Details

This function takes the same inputs as Input_Rate() plus the names of one or more category columns in dfNumerator and/or dfDenominator. For each group and category it counts the numerator (or denominator) records that fall in that category. The Total of each breakdown is the group's numerator (or denominator) as calculated by Input_Rate(), so the breakdowns reconcile with the metric by construction.

Data Specification

dfSubjects, dfNumerator and dfDenominator must meet the requirements of Input_Rate(). In addition, every column named in strNumeratorCatCols must exist in dfNumerator, and every column named in strDenominatorCatCols must exist in dfDenominator.

Category values are counted as follows:

  • Each category row is assigned to its subject's group via dfSubjects. Rows for subjects that are not in dfSubjects, or whose group is missing, are dropped, exactly as in Input_Rate().

  • When strCatDelim is supplied, multi-value cells (e.g. "EXCL07|INCL06") are split on the delimiter and trimmed. A record then counts once in each of its categories; repeated values within one cell count once. For these variables, the category counts can add up to more than Total. strCatDelim applies to every category column.

  • Missing and blank values are reported as the category "Not recorded".

  • Every group receives a row for every category observed anywhere in the data for that source and variable. Categories that a group does not have are reported with Count = 0 and Participants = 0.

  • Count uses the same method as the corresponding Input_Rate() side: with "Count" it is the number of records in the category; with "Sum" it is the sum of strNumeratorCol / strDenominatorCol in the category. Participants is the number of distinct subjects in the category.

Examples

# Break down AEs by seriousness and participants by IP non-starter status,
# per site
dfDist <- Input_Rate_Dist(
  dfSubjects = gsm.core::lSource$Raw_SUBJ,
  dfNumerator = gsm.core::lSource$Raw_AE,
  dfDenominator = gsm.core::lSource$Raw_SUBJ,
  strSubjectCol = "subjid",
  strGroupCol = "invid",
  strGroupLevel = "Site",
  strNumeratorMethod = "Count",
  strDenominatorMethod = "Count",
  strNumeratorCatCols = "aeser",
  strDenominatorCatCols = "drv_ip_nonstarter_status"
)
